outcome: Symptoms of eating disorders (measured by Eating Disorders Inventory-2)
cohort: 50 puerperae (25 obese and 25 normal-weight, matched for parity and delivery route)
finding: Although none of the scores fell in the pathological range, obese mothers had more pronounced symptoms of eating disorders compared to normal-weight mothers, but they were also more likely to maintain full breastfeeding at 6 months postpartum.
mod_finding: While mode of delivery did not differ between obese and normal-weight mothers, obese mothers were more likely to maintain full breastfeeding at 6 months.
